## Claim being audited

This is a fresh-tablet construction plan for all ten configured claims. The manuscript naturally decomposes into three branches: (A) fronts, locally constant multi-sequences, and Nash-Williams; (B) generalized shifts on increasing self-embeddings of the naturals; and (C) the iterated nonempty powerset and its hereditarily countable part. There is no defect in the paper that prevents formalization, but branch C must preserve the paper's genuinely iterated, well-founded hierarchy rather than silently replacing it by the first-level type `Set Q`.

## Foundational interfaces

Use Mathlib's unbundled `WellQuasiOrdered r` for the paper's sequence definition of wqo, with an explicit `IsPreorder` assumption on `r` when order laws are needed. Represent an infinite subset of the naturals by an increasing order embedding `IncSeq := Nat ↪o Nat`. This single type also represents the paper's monoid `IIf`; composition is the monoid action, and shift is right-composition with successor. Define finite-prefix agreement and `LocallyConstant` directly: a value at `x` is decided by some finite prefix of `x`. This is equivalent to continuity into a discrete type in the Baire subspace topology, but keeps all combinatorial proofs independent of general topology. State and prove closure under composition and restriction early.

For fronts, use the paper's explicit definition (paper lines 1078-1090), over finite strictly increasing lists or an equivalent finite-set-with-prefix representation. A `Front X` must carry a prefix-free family and the density/bar property against every subsequence of the base `X`, including the exceptional trivial front `{empty}`. Define restriction to a subsequence, rays, the prefix tree, sub-front, super-sequence, and the shift relation on finite members. Prove uniqueness of the front member that is a proper prefix of an infinite sequence, restriction remains a front, rays remain fronts, and the prefix tree is well-founded. The Nash-Williams proof can then recurse on accessibility in this tree; an explicit ordinal-valued rank is not needed. Its fusion step also needs the elementary infinite pigeonhole lemma for a Boolean sequence.

For topological digraphs, use a small structure or predicate for a prefix-continuous relation homomorphism. Define continuous-homomorphic reducibility, `BetterRel r` as absence of a prefix-continuous homomorphism from shift into the complement of `r`, and `GBetter g r` analogously with right-composition by `g`. Define `Bqo r` by the paper's equivalent bad locally constant multi-sequence clause (lines 1445-1459), and later prove the super-sequence equivalence rather than taking it as a second definition.

For the full hierarchy, use a universe-polymorphic tagged PSet-style inductive type: an atom `q : Q`, or a nonempty family of earlier trees indexed by an arbitrary small type. Define the lifted relation by exactly the four clauses at paper lines 1404-1419. Raw well-founded tree codes may be used instead of an extensional quotient because mutually extensional codes are equivalent in this quasi-order, but that equivalence and invariance must be proved. Define hereditary countability recursively by countability of every node's index type. This preserves arbitrary well-founded iteration; `Set Q` is reserved for the separate first-powerset Rado theorem.

## Intended DAG

```text
IncSeq + prefix/local constancy + WQO
  |-- orbit/block arithmetic --> RmapLemma + EmapLemma --> MainProp
  |                                               |--> g-BQO --> lines 1748-1753
  |-- Front core --> restriction/ray/tree-WF --> NashWilliams
  |                                      |--> finite-color front theorem --> SuperNW
  |                                      |--> fixed-arity Ramsey (n=3,4) --> Rado embedding
  |-- Front core + local constancy --> super/multi bridge --+
  |                                                         + NashWilliams --> perfect/bad dichotomy --> subarr
  |-- Bqo core + iterated Power tree/order/game --> bad-map reflection --> PowerQPresBqo
                                                        |
  Front tree-WF + bad-super bridge --> ConverseGame ----+--> HerCtblWqo
  HerCtbl countable-node closure + WQO/WF lemmas ------------> HerCtblWellF
```

The generalized-shift branch should split `RmapLemma` from `EmapLemma`. For nonidentity `g`, first prove the least moved point exists, all smaller points are fixed, every increasing injection satisfies `n <= f n`, and the orbit `G(n)=g^[n](k_g)` is strictly increasing and unbounded. `RmapLemma` is restriction along `G`. For `EmapLemma`, isolate the unique orbit-block decomposition and prove separately that the paper's piecewise sigma is increasing, prefix-continuous, and satisfies `sigma(f after succ)=sigma(f) after g` (paper lines 1787-1835). `MainProp` is then just the pair of homomorphisms.

Nash-Williams should be proved before developing any independent infinite Ramsey library. The fixed-length fronts give exactly the homogeneous triple and quadruple instances used in the proof of the target at lines 985-987. For that target, separately define Rado's order, domination on `Set Q`, bad sequences of pairs, the witness-selection lemma from a bad powerset sequence, and the two thinning lemmas. The final map must reflect as well as preserve Rado's order; proving only monotonicity is insufficient.

The multi-sequence branch should construct the minimal deciding front of a locally constant finite coloring (paper lines 1277-1289), apply Nash-Williams, and obtain the perfect-versus-bad dichotomy specialized to shift. This is enough for all three implications in `lem:subarr`; do not record only the one implication written out at lines 1660-1662. In particular, prove transport of badness and perfectness through the super/multi correspondence and through restriction.

The powerset-preservation node must sit above a substantive reflection theorem matching paper lines 1533-1550: a bad locally constant map into the full iterated hierarchy yields a bad locally constant map into the atoms. Build the finite descending comparison game, prove termination from structural well-foundedness, prove the four-clause order is equivalent to a winning strategy for player II and its negation to one for player I, then formalize the diagonal copying construction. Do not introduce the final preservation theorem until these interfaces have complete natural-language proofs.

For `HerCtblQ`, prove both directions in paper lines 1585-1590. Forward uses powerset preservation, bqo implies wqo, and heredity to the countable subtype. Reverse uses a bad super-sequence, well-founded recursion on its front tree to form the countably branching `tilde f`, and `ConverseGame`. For the well-founded characterization, one direction is Mathlib's wqo-implies-well-founded strict part. The converse is special to `HerCtblQ`: from a bad sequence, form the countable nonempty nodes of its successive tails and obtain a strict descending chain. Do not use the false general statement that every well-founded preorder is wqo.

## Target order

Reach targets in this order: (1) `MainProp`; (2) `g-BQO`; (3) `lines:1748-1753`; (4) `cor:NashWill`; (5) `corollary:SuperNW`; (6) `lem:subarr`; (7) `lines:985-987`; (8) `cor PowerQPresBqo`; (9) `thm BqoHerCtblWqo`; (10) `thm BqoHerCtblWellF`. The first three give an early, relatively independent closed branch. Nash-Williams then supplies both the front results and the finite Ramsey thinning used by Laver's theorem. The iterated-powerset results come last because their game/reflection infrastructure is the deepest part of the manuscript.

Each mathematical concept above should be its own paired node; do not stack helper claims in one ordinary `.tex` file. Every proof-bearing node needs a complete proof block, and dependencies should cite principal nodes only. Keep imports above the tablet marker and the unique `-- BODY` marker immediately after the principal declaration's body delimiter.

audit_plan.report:
## Claim being audited

This is a fresh-tablet construction plan for all ten configured claims. The manuscript naturally decomposes into three branches: (A) fronts, locally constant multi-sequences, and Nash-Williams; (B) generalized shifts on increasing self-embeddings of the naturals; and (C) the iterated nonempty powerset and its hereditarily countable part. There is no defect in the paper that prevents formalization, but branch C must preserve the paper's genuinely iterated, well-founded hierarchy rather than silently replacing it by the first-level type `Set Q`.

## Foundational interfaces

Use Mathlib's unbundled `WellQuasiOrdered r` for the paper's sequence definition of wqo, with an explicit `IsPreorder` assumption on `r` when order laws are needed. Represent an infinite subset of the naturals by an increasing order embedding `IncSeq := Nat ↪o Nat`. This single type also represents the paper's monoid `IIf`; composition is the monoid action, and shift is right-composition with successor. Define finite-prefix agreement and `LocallyConstant` directly: a value at `x` is decided by some finite prefix of `x`. This is equivalent to continuity into a discrete type in the Baire subspace topology, but keeps all combinatorial proofs independent of general topology. State and prove closure under composition and restriction early.

For fronts, use the paper's explicit definition (paper lines 1078-1090), over finite strictly increasing lists or an equivalent finite-set-with-prefix representation. A `Front X` must carry a prefix-free family and the density/bar property against every subsequence of the base `X`, including the exceptional trivial front `{empty}`. Define restriction to a subsequence, rays, the prefix tree, sub-front, super-sequence, and the shift relation on finite members. Prove uniqueness of the front member that is a proper prefix of an infinite sequence, restriction remains a front, rays remain fronts, and the prefix tree is well-founded. The Nash-Williams proof can then recurse on accessibility in this tree; an explicit ordinal-valued rank is not needed. Its fusion step also needs the elementary infinite pigeonhole lemma for a Boolean sequence.

For topological digraphs, use a small structure or predicate for a prefix-continuous relation homomorphism. Define continuous-homomorphic reducibility, `BetterRel r` as absence of a prefix-continuous homomorphism from shift into the complement of `r`, and `GBetter g r` analogously with right-composition by `g`. Define `Bqo r` by the paper's equivalent bad locally constant multi-sequence clause (lines 1445-1459), and later prove the super-sequence equivalence rather than taking it as a second definition.

For the full hierarchy, use a universe-polymorphic tagged PSet-style inductive type: an atom `q : Q`, or a nonempty family of earlier trees indexed by an arbitrary small type. Define the lifted relation by exactly the four clauses at paper lines 1404-1419. Raw well-founded tree codes may be used instead of an extensional quotient because mutually extensional codes are equivalent in this quasi-order, but that equivalence and invariance must be proved. Define hereditary countability recursively by countability of every node's index type. This preserves arbitrary well-founded iteration; `Set Q` is reserved for the separate first-powerset Rado theorem.

## Intended DAG

```text
IncSeq + prefix/local constancy + WQO
  |-- orbit/block arithmetic --> RmapLemma + EmapLemma --> MainProp
  |                                               |--> g-BQO --> lines 1748-1753
  |-- Front core --> restriction/ray/tree-WF --> NashWilliams
  |                                      |--> finite-color front theorem --> SuperNW
  |                                      |--> fixed-arity Ramsey (n=3,4) --> Rado embedding
  |-- Front core + local constancy --> super/multi bridge --+
  |                                                         + NashWilliams --> perfect/bad dichotomy --> subarr
  |-- Bqo core + iterated Power tree/order/game --> bad-map reflection --> PowerQPresBqo
                                                        |
  Front tree-WF + bad-super bridge --> ConverseGame ----+--> HerCtblWqo
  HerCtbl countable-node closure + WQO/WF lemmas ------------> HerCtblWellF
```

The generalized-shift branch should split `RmapLemma` from `EmapLemma`. For nonidentity `g`, first prove the least moved point exists, all smaller points are fixed, every increasing injection satisfies `n <= f n`, and the orbit `G(n)=g^[n](k_g)` is strictly increasing and unbounded. `RmapLemma` is restriction along `G`. For `EmapLemma`, isolate the unique orbit-block decomposition and prove separately that the paper's piecewise sigma is increasing, prefix-continuous, and satisfies `sigma(f after succ)=sigma(f) after g` (paper lines 1787-1835). `MainProp` is then just the pair of homomorphisms.

Nash-Williams should be proved before developing any independent infinite Ramsey library. The fixed-length fronts give exactly the homogeneous triple and quadruple instances used in the proof of the target at lines 985-987. For that target, separately define Rado's order, domination on `Set Q`, bad sequences of pairs, the witness-selection lemma from a bad powerset sequence, and the two thinning lemmas. The final map must reflect as well as preserve Rado's order; proving only monotonicity is insufficient.

The multi-sequence branch should construct the minimal deciding front of a locally constant finite coloring (paper lines 1277-1289), apply Nash-Williams, and obtain the perfect-versus-bad dichotomy specialized to shift. This is enough for all three implications in `lem:subarr`; do not record only the one implication written out at lines 1660-1662. In particular, prove transport of badness and perfectness through the super/multi correspondence and through restriction.

The powerset-preservation node must sit above a substantive reflection theorem matching paper lines 1533-1550: a bad locally constant map into the full iterated hierarchy yields a bad locally constant map into the atoms. Build the finite descending comparison game, prove termination from structural well-foundedness, prove the four-clause order is equivalent to a winning strategy for player II and its negation to one for player I, then formalize the diagonal copying construction. Do not introduce the final preservation theorem until these interfaces have complete natural-language proofs.

For `HerCtblQ`, prove both directions in paper lines 1585-1590. Forward uses powerset preservation, bqo implies wqo, and heredity to the countable subtype. Reverse uses a bad super-sequence, well-founded recursion on its front tree to form the countably branching `tilde f`, and `ConverseGame`. For the well-founded characterization, one direction is Mathlib's wqo-implies-well-founded strict part. The converse is special to `HerCtblQ`: from a bad sequence, form the countable nonempty nodes of its successive tails and obtain a strict descending chain. Do not use the false general statement that every well-founded preorder is wqo.

## Target order

Reach targets in this order: (1) `MainProp`; (2) `g-BQO`; (3) `lines:1748-1753`; (4) `cor:NashWill`; (5) `corollary:SuperNW`; (6) `lem:subarr`; (7) `lines:985-987`; (8) `cor PowerQPresBqo`; (9) `thm BqoHerCtblWqo`; (10) `thm BqoHerCtblWellF`. The first three give an early, relatively independent closed branch. Nash-Williams then supplies both the front results and the finite Ramsey thinning used by Laver's theorem. The iterated-powerset results come last because their game/reflection infrastructure is the deepest part of the manuscript.

Each mathematical concept above should be its own paired node; do not stack helper claims in one ordinary `.tex` file. Every proof-bearing node needs a complete proof block, and dependencies should cite principal nodes only. Keep imports above the tablet marker and the unique `-- BODY` marker immediately after the principal declaration's body delimiter.
